'''''Aeonium undulatum''''' is a [[succulent plant|succulent]], [[evergreen]] [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]].  It is a [[subshrub]], one of the larger [[species]] of ''[[Aeonium]]'' with an {{convert|8|-|12|in}} [[rosette (botany)|rosette]] of bright, glossy green [[Leaf|leaves]]<ref>{{Cite web|last=susan.mahr|title=Aeonium|url=https://hort.extension.wisc.edu/articles/aeonium/|access-date=2021-04-12|website=Wisconsin Horticulture|language=en-US}}</ref> often over a metre from the ground on a single, unbranched stem.<ref name="tropicalbritain">{{Cite web|title=Aeonium undulatum|url=https://www.tropicalbritain.co.uk/aeonium-undulatum.html|access-date=2021-04-12|website=www.tropicalbritain.co.uk|language=en}}</ref>  Other rosettes do not branch off this stem (normally) but grow from the bottom, unlike most aeoniums. The plant is [[monocarpic]] so the flowering stem will die after producing its yellow [[inflorescence]], which is normally after about 5 years.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aeonium undulatum (Stalked Aeonium)|url=http://succulents.today/aeonium-undulatum-stalked-aeonium/|access-date=2021-04-12|website=Succulents.today|language=en-US}}</ref>

''Aeonium undulatum'' is [[native plant|native]] and [[endemism|endemic]] to Gran Canaria in the Canary islands.<ref name=Bramwell>{{cite book|last1=Bramwell|first1=D.|last2=Bramwell|first2=Z.|year=2001|title=Wild flowers of the Canary Islands|publisher=Editorial Rueda|location=Madrid, Spain|ISBN=84-7207-129-4}}</ref>{{rp|167}}

The Latin [[specific epithet]] ''undulatum'' means "wavy", and refers to the leaf shape.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=184533731X }}</ref><ref>{{in lang|es}} [http://www.floradecanarias.com/aeonium_undulatum.html Flora Vascular de Canarias]</ref> The common name "saucer plant" is applied to this and other plants of a similar habit.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Aeonium_undulatum.html |title=Desert Tropicals |access-date=2009-04-29 |archive-date=2009-05-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090531013619/http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Aeonium_undulatum.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In [[temperate region]]s this plant may be grown under glass, in a suitable cactus compost.<!--AGM withdrawn It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].--><ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Aeonium undulatum'' | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/77251/Aeonium-undulatum/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> It prefers full sun to part shade and requires excellent drainage.<ref name="tropicalbritain" /> In the [[United States|US]], it may be grown outside in [[Hardiness zone|zones]] 10 and 11.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aeonium undulatum - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279527&isprofile=0&|access-date=2021-04-12|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref>
